prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the passenger in a rear-end collision in Conroe, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1065; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Can you please state your full name for the record?

A: I'd rather just be referred to as the claimant, if that's okay.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was riding in the front passenger seat of a sedan. We were stopped at a red light on the main road in Conroe, Texas, near the shopping center.

Q: And what happened next?

A: The driver behind us didn't stop in time. I felt a hard jolt from behind, and my head snapped back and then forward. My right hand hit the dashboard when we lurched.

Q: Did you lose consciousness or hit your head?

A: No, I didn't black out. I was dizzy for a few minutes, but I stayed awake the whole time.

Q: Did you get medical attention right away?

A: Yes, the paramedics checked me at the scene, and then I went to the emergency room that same afternoon. They X-rayed my wrist and said it was fractured. They put it in a splint and I had a follow-up with an orthopedic doctor later that week.

Q: Are you still receiving treatment for the wrist?

A: Yes. I'm in a cast right now, and I have physical therapy twice a week. The doctor says I may need more therapy before I regain full grip strength.

Q: Have you missed any time from work because of the injury?

A: Yes, I've been out for several weeks. I work with my hands, so I can't do most of my duties with the cast on.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that my neck has been sore since the accident, and I'm still following up on that with my doctor.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
